title: Roman calumny: Reformed allegedly teach only covering, not real removal
source_text: XXIV. Atque haec sententiae orthodoxae explicatio probe tenenda & observanda est, propter Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, qui nostros exagitant, quasi docerent in justificatis non tolli peccata, sed tantum tegi & non imputari: adeoque hominem, etiam post justificationem, manere in se immundum, injustum & impium, & solum censeri pro justo, pio & mundo, propter alienam justitiam ipsi imputatam: ac proinde omnia justificatorum opera esse immunda, spurca & inquinata, imo peccata mortalia, tametsi non obsint illis, quia per Christi justitiam teguntur & occultantur, ut videre licet apud Becanum Jesuitam, in Summa Theologiae Scholasticae, tom. 2. tract. 4. cap. 2. cujus titulus est, de Justificatione ex sententia Calvinistarum: & apud Gabr. Vasquez tom. 2. in 1. 2. disputat. 202. cap. 4. ubi affirmat haereticos, quos vocat, dogmatizare quod in justificatis peccata non vere tollantur atque eradicentur, sed maneant, quamvis tecta & occultata.
pass_a_gloss: And this explanation of the orthodox opinion is carefully to be held and observed, because of the Doctors of the Roman Church, who harry ours as if they taught that in the justified sins are not taken away but only covered and not imputed: and so that a man, even after justification, remains in himself unclean, unjust, and impious, and is only counted for just, pious, and clean because of an alien righteousness imputed to him: and accordingly that all the works of the justified are unclean, filthy, and polluted, even mortal sins, although they do not hinder them, because through Christ's righteousness they are covered and hidden, as may be seen in Becanus the Jesuit, in the Summa of Scholastic Theology, tome 2, treatise 4, chapter 2, whose title is On Justification according to the opinion of the Calvinists; and in Gabriel Vasquez, tome 2 on 1.2, disputation 202, chapter 4, where he affirms that the heretics, as he calls them, dogmatize that in the justified sins are not truly taken away and eradicated, but remain, though covered and hidden.
pass_b_english: Rome (Becanus, Vasquez) charges that Reformed leave the justified inwardly unclean with only alien cover, even mortal works hidden.
Hold the orthodox explanation against that calumny.
